evidence: The hunk makes subscription unprobed while the reduce `ok = probed.length === 0 || probed.some(r => r.healthy)` drops skipped configs, so [skipped subscription, dead api-key] yields ok:false; the agent's #112 fix `results.some(r => r.skipped || r.healthy)` matches the reviewer's suggestion.
guidance_note: When a change adds a new value to an enum that feeds an aggregate (here a new 'skipped' source), re-derive the aggregate's truth table for mixed inputs, not just the all-one-kind case, before shipping.

evidence: Duplicate of F1 in the same round: same reduce, same mixed-chain trigger, same proposed `probed.some(healthy) || results.some(skipped)`; fixed by the same #112 expression.

`AUTH_FIELDS[auth.method]` can be undefined only if two in-repo enumerations drift, which a test already polices, so the crash is latent rather than reachable; the agent removed the table in #113 instead of guarding the dereference.
guidance_note: When a lookup keyed by one enumeration is indexed by values from another, derive one table from the other at design time so no drift test or guard is needed.

evidence: PROVIDERS is a static in-repo table, so a per-run check re-validates a constant (pushback holds), but the parity claim rested on a test only; the agent declined the runtime check and moved the invariant into module-load `assertPresetsSafe` in #113.

Same false-block as F1; the reviewer proposed honoring only a skipped primary (`results[0]?.skipped`), the agent used `results.some(skipped || healthy)`, which also passes [dead primary, skipped fallback] and the packet does not show whether failover reaches a fallback after a non-transient primary failure.

The hunk's `if (auth.method === 'subscription') return true` routes list price into the spend ledger; the agent agreed but deferred to ticket zai-billing-xl0.2 (landed as #114) because DAILY_BUDGET_USD is unset by default, a defensible scoping call.

Both crashes need an in-repo adapter to omit or drift its declaration, a code-change-only state; the agent's #113 deletion of AUTH_FIELDS removes the second, and the reply does not address the missing-`authMethods` `.join` half.

The new `--base-url` refusal and subscription label branch in scripts/local-review.js had no tests; the agent added three in #113, but those tests matched only the literal provider name, which #113/F5 later showed misses the default `auto` alias.
guidance_note: When adding a guard on a provider name, write its tests through every alias that resolves to that name, including the default.

evidence: Same skipped-config false-block as F1; the reviewer suggested keying on the selected/first config, the agent used the any-skipped-or-healthy reduce in #112.
Fourth duplicate of the F1 false-block in the same round, proposing the exact reduce the agent shipped in #112.
The edited CLAUDE.md line listed `OPENAI_* / ZAI_* / CLAUDE_*` while DeepSeek, then the default provider, reads DEEPSEEK_*; the agent added it in #110.
guidance_note: When editing an enumerated list in docs, regenerate it from the code's actual input set rather than appending the new item.

narrative: Single-round review of the auth-union refactor that raised the preflight false-block five times as near-duplicates. The agent merged the PR about two minutes after the review and then answered every thread hours later, pointing at follow-up PRs: #112 for preflight, #113 for the AUTH_FIELDS/test findings, #110 for the docs line, and a deferred ticket for notional cost. Those follow-ups produced their own fix-caused findings (#112/F2, #112/F4, #113/F2, #114/*).
guidance_observations: The PR merged at 04:04 while the CHANGES_REQUESTED review posted at 04:02 sat unanswered, so every fix shipped in a separate PR that was reviewed on its own, outside this thread.
Five findings on one line describing one bug say the reviewer's convergence step did not dedupe; answering them with one identical reply was right.

evidence: The diff retargets `auto` to claude-subscription and updates only the Quickstart and Providers table; the reviewer names five later README examples that set only DEEPSEEK_API_KEY with no PROVIDER, which now fail at startup on missing CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. The thread is unresolved with no reply.
guidance_note: When retargeting a default alias, grep the docs for every example that relies on the old default's credential and update or pin each one in the same change.

narrative: The PR merged 8 seconds after it was created, before the review posted at 04:17. The one real finding, stale README examples that now break under the retargeted `auto`, got no answer.
guidance_observations: Merging before the reviewer runs turns every finding into an orphaned thread; this one points at a real copy-paste breakage for consumers.

evidence: The new branch returns `gitHubTransport(files)` whenever the unified diff parses to zero files. A Gitea PR with only renames or binaries reaches the same branch, because parseUnifiedDiff drops hunkless files. That sends 'APPROVE' to Gitea, which this file's own comments say sticks at PENDING. Nobody replied, and the PR merged with this open.
guidance_note: Before replacing a throw with a fallback value, list every input that reaches that branch (here GitHub large-file AND Gitea hunkless diffs) and make the fallback correct for each, not just the motivating one.

evidence: The #109/F1 fix `results.some(r => r.skipped || r.healthy)` turns `preflight([])` from ok:true into ok:false, and the comment claims the change 'subsumes' the old special case. The reviewer itself says no caller can reach an empty chain, and failing an empty chain is arguably the better behavior, so a reasoned reply was owed rather than a code change.
guidance_note: When collapsing a special case into one expression, check the empty input against the old expression and state the change in the comment.

evidence: Duplicate of F1: same Gitea rename/binary-only path through `return gitHubTransport(files)` to a PENDING-stuck review, with the fix of carrying host identity through. No reply.
Duplicate of F2: `[].some(...)` is false, so an empty chain now fails where the old `probed.length === 0` clause passed. The reviewer concedes this is unreachable today, and nobody replied.

With every file patchless, `filteredFiles.filter(f => f.patch)` is empty whether or not the files were excluded, so runPrReview approves code no engine read; the old path threw. The agent later conceded this exactly in #115 ('Filtering on `f.patch` here APPROVED the exact case the engine handles') but never answered here.
guidance_note: When a fallback hands an empty set to a downstream that treats empty as 'approve', trace that downstream before declaring the fallback safe.

narrative: This follow-up shipped the #109 preflight fix plus a transport fallback for patchless PRs. It merged at 09:38 against a CHANGES_REQUESTED review from 09:31, with all five threads unanswered. Two of them are fix-caused empty-chain edge cases from the #109/F1 fix. The transport findings were real correctness bugs: the Gitea PENDING-stuck path and the silent approval of unread code. #115 later fixed the silent approval.
guidance_observations: The PR merged over CHANGES_REQUESTED with zero replies, including two duplicated correctness bugs. The address-pr-reviews loop never ran on this PR.

evidence: The hunk changes `f.baseUrl || spec.defaultBaseUrl` to `preset.baseUrl ?? baseUrl ?? preset.defaultBaseUrl`, so an explicit '' override wins. The agent switched to `||`, added a non-empty rule to assertPresetsSafe, and deleted the duplicated action.yml defaults that had masked the bug. That one-source move then produced F14.
guidance_note: When swapping `||` for `??` on input-derived strings, test the empty-string input explicitly, because Actions inputs arrive as '' rather than undefined.

evidence: The agent answered #109/F4 by pointing at module-load `assertPresetsSafe` in this PR, but that check runs once over an exported mutable object. Mutation needs in-process code, the same code-change-only state the agent called non-issue in #109/F4. Freezing inside the enforcer costs nothing, though, and closes the hole.
guidance_note: When an invariant is checked once at load, make the checked object immutable in the same function so 'validated' also means 'unchanged since'.

evidence: Duplicate of F1: same `??` empty-string override, fixed by the same 3be5514 change.
Third copy of the `??` finding. It adds the point that action.yml defaults only masked the bug, and the agent acted on that by deleting them.

The guard compares `opts.provider === 'claude-subscription'` while the default is 'auto', which aliases to claude-subscription since #110. That makes the guard dead in the common case, and the agent admits the old happy-path test asserted the silent drop. This is not a fix-caused finding within the PR: the guard predates it, and the gap opened when #110 retargeted `auto`, not from a review fix.
guidance_note: When retargeting an alias, grep for every literal comparison against the alias's target name and route it through alias resolution.

evidence: This PR renamed the capabilities to `apiTypes`/`credentialKinds`, but CLAUDE.md still said `endpointKinds`.
guidance_note: After a field rename, grep docs for the old identifier in the same commit.

evidence: The CLAUDE.md bullet still named `authMethod` and `AUTH_FROM_INPUTS`, which the hunk shows this PR deleted.
guidance_note: After deleting a symbol, grep docs for its name in the same commit.

evidence: The replaced 1.41.0 note says `apiKeyEnv` was renamed then, but the new 1.43.0 note re-attributes that rename to 1.43.0.
guidance_note: When rewriting a changelog note, list only what this version changed and diff the claim against the note being replaced.

evidence: The test title still says 'carrying NO baseUrl', while the edited assertion now deep-equals an endpoint with the pinned Anthropic baseUrl.
guidance_note: When inverting what a test asserts, rename the test in the same edit.

evidence: An unmapped `credential.kind` can only come from a code change to PRESETS, and the only casualty would be a dev script's label. The agent pinned it with a test that renders formatReport for every PRESETS kind instead of adding a runtime guard, and gave a defensible reason why `authEnv()` keeps its runtime throw.

`supports('endpoint.apiType', preset.apiType, ...)` names a field the preset-form author never wrote. The agent made every call site name the written field plus the resolved value, as the reviewer suggested.
guidance_note: Write validation errors in terms of the key the user wrote, not the value it resolved to.

evidence: The kept comment says an absent baseUrl means Anthropic, while the reviewer reports the new body does `if (!baseUrl) return false`. The agent agreed and rewrote the comment.
guidance_note: When rewriting a function body, reread its header comment against the new branches.

evidence: The test comment describes the deleted auth-union shortcut ('no baseUrl to sniff'), while the fixture now carries a pinned baseUrl and goes through the hostname whitelist.

The F1 fix deleted action.yml's copies of the provider defaults and added a test that action.yml restates none, but README still hardcoded the same values. The agent's reply concedes 'I closed the drift for action.yml and left it open one file over', and the new README test immediately failed on the undocumented pinned host. The flag names 6ddbcd4, a rename-only commit; the cause is the 3be5514 F1 fix.
guidance_note: When fixing a duplicated-fact drift in one file, grep the repo for every other literal copy of the same values and cover them in the same commit.

evidence: The F2 fix froze PRESETS but left PROVIDERS mutable, and `PROVIDERS['claude-subscription'].preset = 'openai'` routes around the freeze. The agent's reply says 'I froze PRESETS last round on exactly this argument and then left the table that routes into it mutable'. The threat model is in-process code, so the premise counts as partly true.
guidance_note: When hardening one table of a security invariant, enumerate every table on the path from input to the protected value (here PROVIDER_ALIASES -> PROVIDERS -> PRESETS) and apply the same hardening to all.

evidence: The F5 fix added `require('../src/provider')` inside parseArgs. At the time that pulled the whole engine stack into the 'pure-helper' tests, breaking the file header's isolation promise. The agent says 'I'd noticed it while writing the guard and shipped it anyway'. The fix moved the base-URL literals into provider.js so the module imports no engine code.
guidance_note: When a fix adds an import, check the importing file's header invariants and the imported module's transitive deps before pushing, and resolve a known contradiction rather than shipping it.

narrative: This credential-pinning redesign also served as the agent's answer to several #109 findings. Round 0 raised 13 findings, mostly stale docs from the redesign and a `??` empty-string regression, all fixed in one commit. Round 1 found nothing. Round 2 found three gaps, each left by a round-0 fix: README still restated the defaults removed from action.yml, PROVIDERS stayed mutable beside the frozen PRESETS, and the alias-aware guard's lazy require pulled in the engine stack. Fixing those cost round 3. F2 also continues a cross-PR chain from #109/F4.
guidance_observations: All three round-2 findings follow one pattern: a fix applied to one instance of a pattern (one file, one table, one import site) without sweeping its siblings.
In F16 the agent saw the contradiction while writing the fix and pushed anyway, which turned a known defect into an extra review round.

evidence: The hunk's `parseCost` returns as soon as `parseMarker(body, NOTIONAL_MARKER_RE)` matches, so a quoted notional marker anywhere beats a trailing dollars marker. That breaks the last-marker-wins quote safety the single-marker parser had. The thread is resolved and outdated, but has no reply, and the packet does not show a fix.
guidance_note: When splitting one marker into two kinds, carry the existing parser's invariants (last occurrence wins) across the union of the kinds and add the cross-kind quoting test the single-kind suite already had.

evidence: Duplicate of F1. It notes that this repo's own tests contain the exact notional marker string, so a self-review quoting it would misclassify real spend. The thread is resolved and outdated with no reply.

`notionalRounds = count + unknownCount` while the message prints `ledger.notional.usd`, which sums only the known entries. The parallel billed branch right above it warns 'LOWER bound', and this one does not. The thread is resolved and outdated with no reply.
guidance_note: When adding a sibling branch to an existing one (notional beside billed), copy over every caveat the original branch carries, here the unknown-count lower-bound warning.

evidence: The new log says 'excluded from the $X spend above', but the only earlier output is the conditional unknown-count warning. The packet does not show the later 'spent today' summary line the reviewer places at ~225, so the ordering claim cannot be confirmed.

The hunk adds a `basis === 'dollars'` discriminator to the eval `costUsd`. The reviewer says test/eval-score.test.js only exercises the dollars basis, but the packet does not include that test file to confirm it. The thread is resolved but not outdated, with no reply.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a discriminator to a value, add a test at every consumer of that value feeding each non-default variant.

narrative: This PR is the deferred fix for #109/F6, splitting cost into dollars, subscription and unpriced bases. Its one review found real gaps in that fix: cross-kind marker parsing lost the last-marker-wins quote safety, and the notional log omits the unknown-count caveat. All five threads were resolved with no reply, and four are outdated, so whether and how each was fixed is not visible in the packet.
guidance_observations: Threads resolved silently leave no record of plan or fix SHA, so the audit cannot tell a fix from a dismissal.

evidence: The agent quotes CLAUDE.md's rule that any consumer-visible change is a minor, and a gate that now spawns an engine instead of approving is one, so the reviewer's generic semver 'patch' reading is wrong. The 1.48.x gap is explained by open PR #120 claiming 1.48.0. The agent kept 1.49.0 and fixed the stale CONTRIBUTING.md release section the reviewer had relied on.
guidance_note: When a version number deliberately skips one claimed by a sibling PR, state that in the PR description at creation, since the reviewer cannot see other branches.

evidence: This re-raises F1 with the single-step rule, which is true. The reviewer admits it 'could not verify ... whether 1.48.0 was already tagged elsewhere'. The agent's merge-order analysis holds: identical `1.47.2 -> 1.48.0` edits auto-merge and silently drop a bump. This is not fix-caused, because the round-1 commit only edited CONTRIBUTING.md and the finding repeats F1 on unchanged package.json.
guidance_note: Put a non-obvious decision's rationale in the PR description on first push, not only in a thread reply, so the next round's reviewer sees it.

evidence: This PR fixes the silent approval of all-patchless PRs that #112/F5 reported. The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive: a00a2bf only touched CONTRIBUTING.md, and the gate change dates from round 0. Within the PR, though, it is the same gap: `diffChurn` still treats a patchless file as zero churn, so difficulty and budget scaling under-size exactly these PRs. The agent deferred it to zai-coverage-rvz, defensibly since both levers default off and Gitea records carry no size fields.
guidance_note: When changing what a missing `patch` means at one consumer, grep every other reader of `f.patch` and decide its meaning in the same change or file it.

narrative: This PR fixes #112's silent approval of all-patchless PRs. Rounds 0 and 1 argued over the 1.49.0 version. The agent was right on both the level and the skip, and turned the first round into a real fix of stale CONTRIBUTING.md release docs. Round 2 found that diffChurn under-sizes patchless files, the same patchless-means-empty assumption in another consumer, and it was deferred to a filed ticket.
guidance_observations: The version rationale went into the PR description only after the second round. Writing it there at creation would likely have avoided the re-raise in round 1.
Five issue comments tracked version collisions by hand across PRs #116-#120, which shows the version-bump gate cannot see sibling PRs.
